info.title: Correlation to Recommendation v1 — mapping approved, activation pending
info.description: The user approved this HTTP mapping and restricted comparison for an isolated Java client on 2026-11-17. Runtime activation remains blocked on authority/reference validation, request/response/member/deadline budgets and overflow disposition. The candidate filename records the artifact origin; it does not authorize a receiving endpoint or deployment.

x-pipesor-pending-decisions: Trusted authority supplier, issuer/audience/role/caller values, current reauthorization and revocation treatment.

Request/response byte limits; protected field sizes; cumulative evidence/signal count; total operation deadline and retry schedule; and disposition when a growing revision exceeds the accepted budget, before preparation. No RAG query or NLP client limit is adopted. No truncation, member loss, window, group split or infinite retry is inferred.
x-pipesor-invariants: operation_id equals context.id and Idempotency-Key. X-Correlation-ID equals context.correlation_id.

Signal evidence IDs are unique and exactly equal context.evidence_ids. Signal order is introduction order, not lexical order. A receiver cannot prove historical order or owner existence from JSON shape.
Every replay/read/delivery must be currently authorized independently of the historical scope envelope. No protected cached result is returned before authorization.
Confirmation requires a complete valid 200 JSON receipt with matching IDs and accepted or duplicate. Non-JSON, empty 200, unknown status or mismatched IDs cannot confirm delivery.
Timeout, connection failure or an ambiguous 5xx leaves reception unknown; recover the same operation and historical representation. No retry budget is selected here.
Do not follow redirects with bearer credentials. Receipt durability does not introduce a background worker, queue or eventual diagnosis guarantee.
Serialize context.correlation_id from the original snapshot. An alias or retry message correlation ID must not replace it; each signal preserves its incorporation correlation ID.

Introducing context IDs are unique; the last signal origin_context_id equals context.id and its correlation_id equals context.correlation_id. These are structural consequences of one new member per snapshot, not proof of owner existence or earlier historical order.

post.description: Proposed single synchronous handoff on the existing relationship; no second component delivery or evidence-fetch API.

parameters.description: Optional W3C technical trace context; not operation identity, authorization evidence or fingerprint input.

200.description: After atomic durable commit: accepted or matching duplicate. Receipt IDs must match the sent operation and context. This is not completed diagnosis.

400.description: Invalid or incompatible contract; no durable acceptance. Proposed permanent rejection.

401.description: Caller authentication failed; no receipt or protected context disclosure. Do not retry unchanged credentials.

403.description: Caller/resource authorization failed; no receipt or existence disclosure. Do not infer a new grant.

409.description: An existing operation/context conflicts with significant content. No effects and no new operation ID.

413.description: Request exceeds a pending explicitly agreed limit. No silent truncation; no automatic retry of unchanged content.

429.description: Capacity unavailable. Delay/retry count and total deadline remain pending; no durable receipt is implied.

503.description: Temporary dependency/reception unavailability. Result may be unknown; recover the same immutable operation rather than create another.

entraBearer.description: Entra app-only identity. Real issuer, audience, role, caller binding and resource authority remain unresolved; no placeholder values grant access.

ProtectedText.description: Already minimized and protected text. Shape validation is not sanitization; exact whitespace and Unicode are preserved. U+0000 is excluded because the receiving PostgreSQL text/JSON representation cannot retain it.

evidence_ids.description: Proposed lexical canonical UUID order in the wire copy only. The persisted snapshot is a set and may use Java UUID ordering; do not mutate it to encode the request. Signals retain introduction order.

created_at.description: Proposed canonical UTC representation of the existing technical snapshot timestamp; six fractional digits preserve PostgreSQL microseconds.

signals.description: Exactly one protected signal per evidence ID, in original introduction order. No later members, template, raw body or new source timestamps.

x-pipesor-approval.scope: HTTP mapping, strict compatibility and restricted comparison; isolated Java client only

x-pipesor-comparison.scope: Only the validated Submission JSON body, including business correlation, historical scope, snapshot and exact ordered signals. Never reuse the NLP input_fingerprint.
x-pipesor-comparison.rendering: Reject duplicate JSON keys, non-JSON numeric constants, unpaired Unicode surrogates, noncanonical UUIDs, timestamp shape, unsorted wire evidence IDs and unknown fields first. No UTF-8 BOM. Preserve all string code points and whitespace: no trim or Unicode normalization. Sort object keys (all schema keys are ASCII); emit compact JSON with no insignificant spaces, UTF-8 and non-ASCII characters unescaped. Escape quote and backslash; use \b, \t, \n, \f and \r for those C0 controls and lowercase \u00xx for the remaining C0 controls. Preserve array order; pipeline_id is explicitly present even when null. Golden canonical strings/UTF-8 hashes are in the companion synthetic examples.
x-pipesor-comparison.fingerprint: v1:sha256: followed by lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the defined bytes. HTTP Authorization and W3C trace headers are excluded. The example metadata retains its original proposed_* names for traceability; these are not wire fields.
